item.title: How Custom Packaging Cost Actually Works When You're Scaling a Brand
item.description:
What goes into a custom packaging quote, how volume changes your per-unit cost, and how to build a packaging budget you can plan around - from your first order to your next reorder.

The Tendlyn Team

If you’re preparing for a product launch or scaling an existing line, packaging cost is one of the first budget items you’ll need to pin down. The challenge is that a per-unit price on a quote doesn’t tell you much on its own - it’s the result of several variables interacting at once, and understanding those variables is what makes packaging budgeting feel manageable instead of unpredictable.

item.title: Kraft vs White Custom Mailer Boxes: Which Material Is Right for Your Brand?
item.description:
One substrate adds warmth before you print a single color. The other gives your design nowhere to hide. Here’s how to choose the right one for your mailer box.

The Tendlyn Team

The outer surface of a mailer box is the first physical thing a customer touches when an order arrives. Before they read your logo or pull the tape, the material itself already says something about your brand. Choosing between a kraft and white substrate isn’t simply a color preference – it affects how your print looks, how your brand is perceived, and how well the box aligns with your brand’s visual identity. Here’s how to think through that decision clearly.

item.title: Paperboard vs. Corrugated: How to Choose the Right Material for Your Product Box
item.description:
Paperboard delivers polished print and shelf appeal, while corrugated adds shipping strength. Learn when to use each - and when your packaging needs both.

The tendlyn Team
The tendlyn Team

Paperboard vs. Corrugated: How to Choose the Right Material for Your Product Box

A folding carton and a corrugated mailer may both be paper-based, but they are engineered for different jobs. Paperboard provides a smooth print surface and a compact format that works well on retail shelves. Corrugated board adds a fluted layer that helps packaging withstand stacking, handling, and shipping.

item.title: Where to Customize Printed Packaging Boxes for Cosmetics and Beauty Brands at Scale
item.description:
Cosmetic packaging boxes have to protect fragile products while carrying mandatory label information and presenting product colors accurately both online and in physical stores. Glass bottles, pump dispensers, droppers, detailed ingredient lists, and shade-sensitive artwork all add design constraints that need to be considered before production begins.

tendlyn works with cosmetic and skincare brands on orders ranging from initial low-volume runs to hundreds of thousands of units. Common procurement questions include how much panel space the required text will take up, which finishing technique best matches the brand positioning, and what a sensible order quantity looks like for an unproven SKU. This guide covers what beauty brands should confirm before requesting packaging quotes.

item.title: 5 Ideas for Environmentally Friendly Packaging
item.description:
Eco friendly packaging can feel like a real minefield - that’s why we are here to simplify matters for businesses! Here are our top 5 environmentally friendly packaging ideas that you can easily adopt.

Read time: 4 mins read

Packaging design can be a challenging process. There are budgetary and practical constraints, and increasingly eco friendly considerations at play as well. For retailers, packaging represents https://www.epa.gov/facts-and-figures-about-materials-waste-and-recycling/containers-and-packaging-product-specific-data

Avoid over-packaging Most packaging designs use far more materials than are actually needed. This has a huge impact on how eco friendly your packaging is overall. For example, if your boxes are too large for your products, you’ll either have to stuff the box with a filler, or risk damaging the item in transit. This is problematic for two reasons: it creates a lot of unnecessary packaging waste, and is an extra expense for your business (the bigger the box, the bigger the bill!). So first things first, you need to refine your product packaging design with the aim to reduce excess. This allows you to cut down on the number of materials used, and to stretch your budget further! Packaging ideas in this area include using smaller boxes, or even dispensing with boxes completely for some orders. If your products are smaller and more resistant to breaking (i.e. clothing or stationery items) then shipping mailers might be a more efficient option. Mailers are one of the cheapest eCommerce packaging elements, and also cost far less than traditional cardboard boxes!
